All first-time authors must get their concepts reviewed (either in the Ideas Critique forum or the IRC chatrooms) and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers before the authors may request feedback on a full draft in the Drafts and Critiques forum. […]

Site members who can greenlight concepts are those who fulfill one or more of the following criteria:

  • They are on the Butterfly Squad Roster list of reviewers.
  • They have an entry in the Authors' Pages list or they qualify1 for an Author Page.
  • They have been featured in the Reviewers' Spotlight.
  • They are a staff member.
Footnotes
1. They have written 3 or more successful mainsite pages.

item.title: Re: NEW DRAFT FORUM POLICIES
item.content:encoded:
Does that also include works on other official branches?

No, the works must be on the English branch.

It doesn't really makes sense for someone with many, sometimes even 10 or 20, established works to need greenlight for me

The greenlighting process is also a check for English writing skills as well, not just strength in conceptualization. Success on one branch is not assumed to automatically translate to success on another branch, especially since the site member audience/community is inherently unique between branches.

That said, anyone can receive draft critique in chat or via private message without needing greenlights. (Some reviewers might still ask for greenlights though, depending on the draft content.)

item.title: Re: NEW DRAFT FORUM POLICIES
item.content:encoded:
So, could I get a list of steps needed to take?

Technically none of the steps are "needed". They're highly recommended, though.

Maybe like: Idea Forum, Draft Forum, … Post article

For a first-time author, the process would be:

  • Ideas Critique forum > obtain two greenlights
  • Draft Critique forum > get multiple positive responses, ideally from experienced reviewers
  • Post to mainsite.

You can swap in IRC chatroom feedback or feedback via private message.

Also are green lights mandatory for people here longer?

Greenlights are required for all first-time authors (i.e., authors who do not yet have a successful mainsite page). It doesn't matter how long they've been a site member; if they're a first-time author, they're a first-time author.

item.content:encoded:
If I get a concept greenlit, is there a time limit on how long that stands for?

Nope!

should I wait until I'm nearly done to seek a pair of greenlights?

Reviewers may very well give you critique that leads to you researching and/or writing differently.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
when can I get my idea greenlit and are you the right person to do so, if so this is my idea so far.

If you want to get your idea greenlit, you should post the summary in the Ideas Critique Forum as a new post rather than here. Then reviewers who meet the greenlighting criteria laid out in the original post here can (if they think your idea works) greenlight it, or at least offer feedback on how you can make it better.

You can also get greenlights via the IRC chatrooms; but it's often handy to have a forum post in that case anyway so you can easily link a reviewer to it to get them up to speed.

item.title: Re: NEW DRAFT FORUM POLICIES
item.content:encoded:
After we get criticism and make edits to our concept, do we post the new concept as a new thread?

Nope! You're correct that this is not the case.

As noted in the ideas forum guidelines (this current conversation is in the draft forum, by the way): authors should not create multiple threads for the same working concept.

Using one thread helps keep spam down, and prevents flooding of the forums with repeat threads. Furthermore, it helps reviewers a lot if all corresponding feedback is kept in one place so they can follow the development of the idea and its details.

GoI formats and tales count as successful pages and allow for bypassing the greenlighting process.

That said, reviewers still may ask that you go through the Ideas Critique forum if a draft's core concept isn't viable enough, so it might be a good idea to get conceptual feedback early on to ensure that the draft will be well-received.
